name: Lumax Industries Ltd
title: Lumax Industries Ltd - 517206 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Lumax FY26 revenue rose 23% to INR 4,184 crore with EBITDA margin at 9.8%; management guides FY27 margin 10.5-11%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 total operating revenue grew 30% y-o-y to INR 1,200 crore, with EBITDA of INR 124.9 crore (10.4% margin, 90 bps forex drag) and PAT of INR 54.1 crore. For FY26, revenue rose 23% to INR 4,184 crore, EBITDA rose 42.8% to INR 412.1 crore at a 9.8% margin, and PAT rose 23.3% to INR 172.5 crore after a one-time INR 17.8 crore labour code charge. Management flagged input cost inflation (raw materials, manpower, energy) and a roughly one-quarter pass-through lag, which it is trying to shorten through monthly price amendments with some OEMs. Order book stands at INR 2,200 crore, 88% LED.

financial_highlights.change: +23.3% y-o-y; includes one-time INR 17.8 crore labour code impact

segments.name: LED lighting
segments.commentary: Over 61% of FY26 revenue versus 58% a year earlier; about 88% of the current order book is LED-based.

segments.name: Passenger vehicles
segments.commentary: 65% of FY26 revenue and nearly two-thirds of the order book.

segments.name: 2-wheelers
segments.commentary: 29% of FY26 revenue; the balance of the order book is mostly 2-wheeler.

segments.name: Product mix
segments.commentary: Front lighting about 69% of FY26 revenue; rear lighting about 22%; remainder other lighting products.

segments.name: Tooling
segments.commentary: Q4 tooling margin was relatively strong; FY26 tooling revenue fell versus FY25 on fewer launches, with a significant rise guided for FY27.

segments.name: JV: SL Lumax
segments.commentary: FY26 turnover around INR 2,900 crore with EBITDA margin close to 14%; supplies Hyundai and opened a new Pune facility.

guidance_outlook: FY27 full-year EBITDA margin guided at 10.5% to 11%, including price recoveries, input costs and tooling profits; management declined a precise FY27 number given volatility.
FY27 management expects margin expansion of about 50 bps or more; medium-term goal close to 13% EBITDA margin in 3-4 years.
FY27 revenue growth guided at least 2x the industry growth rate.
FY27 capex guidance INR 100-150 crore, of which maintenance capex is INR 40-50 crore.
Annual interest cost expected around INR 80 crore for FY27 (from INR 74 crore in FY26).
Effective tax rate expected at 22-23% (statutory 25% regime; deferred tax benefit from capex) in coming years.
Employee cost impact from Haryana minimum wage revision estimated at 30-35 bps; to be passed on to OEMs with a time lag.
Q1 FY27 margin pressure expected across industry; management hopes to maintain guidance but Q1 FY27 vs Q1 FY26 comparison is weaker, with tapering expected later in the year.
capex_capacity: FY26 new capex committed INR 390-400 crore; Bengaluru plant pre-loaded in FY25 and expansion for Maruti and Toyota models on track for commissioning from Q4 FY27.
Phase 2 of Chakan facility commenced operations, primarily serving Skoda and Volkswagen.
FY27 capex INR 100-150 crore, mainly maintenance plus capacity expansion within existing facilities; FY28 capex undecided and dependent on new business wins.
Import content around 25-30% of raw material and bought-out parts.
demand_pricing: Industry: FY26 auto production 34.71 million units (+11.8%); Q4 FY26 production up 19% y-o-y (PV +11%, 2W +21%, 3W +32%, CV +20%).

Order wins: Mahindra XUV 7XO (front fog, cornering, map reading, sun visor, roof lamps); Skoda Kushaq facelift (all tail lamps); Toyota Urban Cruiser Ebella (headlamp, small turn indicator, tail and lid lamps); Suzuki E-Access (2W front turn signal and headlamps).
Maruti revenue grew nearly 50% in FY26 on new model SOPs; healthy growth from Tata Motors and HMSI.
LED penetration: about 60% overall in FY26; over 80% in 2-wheelers, about 60% in passenger cars industry-wide.
Price recovery: pass-through of past price increases received early in Q4; OEM discussions underway on new cost increases, with a one-quarter lag currently.
Inventory about 2-2.1 months; inventory days around 65-70 maintained despite longer LED import lead times.

qa_highlights.question: What employee cost impact is expected from wage hikes in northern and Gujarat plants, and how is it being recovered?
qa_highlights.answer: Haryana revised minimum wages from 1 April 2026, with similar moves in other states. Management estimates a 30-35 bps impact and says it is passing costs to OEMs with a lag, with discussions already started.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 margins hold given input cost volatility and the pass-through lag?
qa_highlights.answer: No precise FY27 guidance given due to volatility. Full-year EBITDA margin still seen at 10.5-11%, with monthly price amendment talks underway with some OEMs to shorten the roughly one-quarter lag.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for mould/tooling revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Tooling revenue tracks new launches; FY26 was lower on fewer launches. A significant increase in tooling revenue is expected in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the industry LED penetration and how far can it go?
qa_highlights.answer: Industry-wide about 60% in passenger cars and over 80% in 2-wheelers; management expects LED share to keep rising over 3-4 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the JV SL Lumax doing?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 turnover around INR 2,900 crore at close to 14% EBITDA margin; expected to grow with industry and keep margins; supplies 100% of Hyundai lamps.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt and interest outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Long-term loan INR 235 crore, of which INR 85-90 crore to be repaid in FY27; no new long-term loans planned. Short-term borrowing to rise with working capital; annual interest cost seen around INR 80 crore for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will working capital stretch in H1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Some temporary increase in working capital days in Q1 and Q2 due to customer recovery lag, normalising later in the year.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation (raw materials, manpower, energy, freight) and whether OEMs accept monthly price amendments; Q1 FY27 margin pressure acknowledged.
West Asia conflict: supply chain disruption, commodity and fuel costs; company holds higher inventory as a buffer.
Forex: 90 bps Q4 and 40 bps FY26 margin drag; import content of 25-30%.
Rising short-term borrowings to fund working capital; interest cost expected to edge up to around INR 80 crore.
Tax rate: effective 22-23% depends on deferred tax, which management says persists while capex continues.
Dependence on OEM programme launches and tooling timing; FY27 tooling revenue step-up needs to materialise.
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY26 records and the order book, but cautious on FY27 margins, which management declined to quantify precisely citing volatility. Answers on pass-through timing and Q1 margins were hedged ("work-in-progress", "hopeful"). Management was clear on capex and debt.
key_quotes: Our order book remains healthy at INR 2,200 crore with LED lighting composition of 88%.
So I would not be in a position to give you an exact guidance for FY 27, considering the volatility.
I think we can safely say that we will at least outperform the industry.
